title: Interactive drivers of root decomposition in restored and natural mangroves
content:
Root decomposition in mangroves is controlled by interactive local factors rather than global factors, highlighting the need for site-specific management strategies. Our results underscore the importance of making site-specific decisions to harness the autochthonous carbon related to mangrove roots effectively. Furthermore, uncertainties in stable carbon isotopes of roots and litter should be carefully considered to better constrain autochthonous carbon. Methodologies for blue carbon credits can be improved by incorporating stable carbon isotopes of roots into isotope mixing models, which can better constrain the contribution of autochthonous carbon.


Abstract

The allocation of blue carbon credits needs to constrain the contribution of autochthonous and allochthonous carbon. In mangroves, live roots turnover to form dead roots, which decompose into autochthonous carbon stored in sediments. However, limited data on root decomposition are available for mangroves, which hinders a comprehensive understanding of carbon dynamics in these ecosystems. This study used 210 litter bags to examine the variation in root decomposition for restored and natural mangroves while considering local environmental factors. This is among the first studies to examine interactive biotic–abiotic drivers of root decomposition in restored mangroves. Data were also combined with published studies on root decomposition to explore global patterns and identify potential drivers of decomposition rate constants. The final remaining root mass was significantly less in restored mangroves due to higher root decomposition rate constants (2.5 × 10−3 ± 2.2 × 10−4 day−1, n = 18) than those in natural mangroves (2.2 × 10−3 ± 3.8 × 10−4 day−1, η 2 = 4 × 10−2, 95% CI: [0, 1], n = 24). Fine roots decompose slower (1.7 × 10–3 ± 1.3 × 10–4 day-1, n = 21) than coarse roots (2.9 × 10−3 ± 4.2 × 10−4 day-1, η 2 = 1.1 × 10−1, 95% CI: [0, 1], n = 21). Fine root decomposition rate constants were also controlled by other local factors, including species, litter C/N, porewater salinity and sediment nutrients. However, no clear pattern was observed for root decomposition rate constants along latitudes and longitudes, suggesting that local factors dominate over global trends. Stable carbon isotopes of roots showed site- and morphology-dependent variation, suggesting distinct decomposition pathways. Synthesis and applications: Root decomposition in mangroves is controlled by interactive local factors rather than global factors, highlighting the need for site-specific management strategies. Our results underscore the importance of making site-specific decisions to harness the autochthonous carbon related to mangrove roots effectively. Furthermore, uncertainties in stable carbon isotopes of roots and litter should be carefully considered to better constrain autochthonous carbon. Methodologies for blue carbon credits can be improved by incorporating stable carbon isotopes of roots into isotope mixing models, which can better constrain the contribution of autochthonous carbon.

摘要

蓝碳碳汇计量需明确区分本地碳源与外来碳源的贡献。在红树林生态系统中, 活体根系周转形成死亡根系, 经分解转化为储存于沉积物中的本地碳。然而, 当前关于红树林根系分解的数据较为匮乏, 限制了对此类生态系统碳动态的全面认知。 本研究通过布设210个凋落物袋, 探究了修复与天然红树林根系分解的差异, 并综合考虑了局地环境因子的影响。这是首批关注修复红树林根系分解过程中生物与非生物因子交互驱动作用的研究之一。同时, 本研究整合了已发表的全球根系分解研究数据, 系统解析分解速率常数的空间格局及其潜在驱动机制。 研究发现:修复红树林的根系分解速率常数(2.5 × 10−3 ± 2.2 × 10−4天−1, n = 18)显著高于天然红树林(2.2 × 10−3 ± 3.8 × 10−4天−1, η 2 = 4 × 10−2, 95% CI: [0, 1], n = 24), 导致其最终残留根系生物量更低；细根分解速率(1.7 × 10−3 ± 1.3 × 10−4天−1, n = 21)显著低于粗根(2.9 × 10−3 ± 4.2 × 10−4天−1, η 2 = 1.1 × 10−1, 95% CI: [0, 1], n = 21)。细根分解速率同时受树种、凋落物碳氮比、孔隙水盐度及沉积物养分等多重局地因子调控。但根系分解速率常数未呈现明显的经纬度梯度格局, 表明局地因子的主导作用超越全球尺度趋势。 根系稳定碳同位素特征呈现显著的样点依赖性与形态差异性, 暗示其分解路径存在分异。 综合启示与应用:红树林根系分解主要受局地因子交互调控而非全球性因子支配, 凸显因地制宜管理策略的重要性。本研究强调, 为有效利用红树林根系相关的本地碳汇, 需制定区域特异性的决策方案。同时, 应审慎评估根系与凋落物稳定碳同位素的不确定性, 以更精准界定本地碳贡献。通过将根系稳定碳同位素纳入同位素混合模型, 可优化蓝碳碳汇计量方法, 从而更准确约束本地碳源的贡献程度。
